stories.headline: India-EU trade deal: cheaper European cars, duty-free Indian textiles
stories.question: What does India get and give up in the EU trade deal due on 16 December?
stories.dek: India gets tariff-free access to Europe for most of its exports, including textiles. In return, it cuts its high duties on European cars and wine. Signing is likely on 16 December, and the deal starts in 2027.

so_far.text: A free trade agreement (FTA) is a deal in which two sides cut tariffs, the taxes they charge on each other's goods. India and the European Union (EU), a bloc of 27 countries, began work on one in 2007. On 27 January 2026 in New Delhi, they finished negotiating a deal billed as the 'mother of all deals'. It still has to be signed and approved.

what_happened.text: In a report published on 22 November 2026, the EU's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, said the India-EU trade pact is likely to be signed on 16 December. That is during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Brussels. He said the deal will come into force in 2027. On 21 November 2026, the EU signed a similar deal with Indonesia in Brussels.

steps.text: A tariff is a tax on imported goods, so high tariffs make foreign products cost more than local ones.
In a trade deal, each side lowers its own tariffs in exchange for the other side lowering theirs.
India wants Europe to drop duties on its exports, such as the 12–17% its textiles now pay.
In return, India opens markets it long protected: cars taxed at up to 110%, wine at up to 150%.
Each side keeps some walls: the EU still shields sugar, rice and milk powders, and gave India no CBAM exemption.

history.text:
The story starts in 2007, when India and the EU began talks on a free trade agreement. Each side would lower its tariffs so the other could sell more. By 2013 the talks had stalled. They stayed stuck until 2022, when both sides relaunched them. The sources do not say why the talks stalled.

The second attempt moved faster. On 27 January 2026, at a summit in New Delhi, the two sides announced that negotiations were concluded. Concluded means the terms are agreed. It does not make the deal law. At the same summit they signed a separate mobility and migration agreement, which covers people moving between India and Europe.

Then came the slow, technical part. Lawyers must check the text, and it must be translated into 23 languages. The Council, where EU governments sit, must approve it, and the European Parliament must give its consent.

The EU was closing other deals at the same time. Its talks with Indonesia concluded in 2025, nearly ten years after they began. That deal was signed in Brussels on 21 November 2026. India's deal is next, and signing is likely on 16 December 2026.

analogy.text: Think of two neighbouring markets that each charge a gate fee on the other's goods. The deal is a swap: both cut most gate fees. But each keeps some gates shut, and India lets only a fixed number of European cars through at the low fee.
analogy.breaks: Real cuts arrive in stages over years, and charges outside the deal, like the EU's carbon charge, still apply.

for_you.text: India's border tax on European cars falls gradually from up to 110% to 10%. On most wines it falls from up to 150% to 30%. Whether shop prices fall depends on sellers. If you work in textiles, EU tariffs of 12–17% disappear. Carbon-heavy exporters still face the EU's carbon charge. Nothing changes before 2027.

misconception.myth: Signing on 16 December means lower tariffs start right away.
misconception.fact: Signing is not the finish line. The European Parliament must consent, the deal comes into force in 2027, and car tariff cuts are gradual.

lesson.concept: How a tariff cut changes an import's price
lesson.big_idea: A tariff is a tax charged as a percentage of an import's value at the border. Cutting the rate cuts the tax, and a quota limits how many goods get the low rate.

steps.title: Start with the border value
steps.text: Every imported good has a value when it reaches India's border: roughly what the importer paid the foreign seller, plus shipping. This value is the base the tariff is charged on.

steps.title: The tariff is a percentage
steps.text: A tariff is a tax set as a percentage of that border value. India's tariff on European cars is up to 110%, so the tax can be bigger than the car's own value.

steps.title: Add them: the landed cost
steps.text: Border value plus tariff gives the landed cost. That is the price before the dealer adds a margin and other taxes. A higher rate means a higher landed cost.

steps.title: A trade deal lowers the rate
steps.text: Under the India-EU deal, the car tariff falls gradually to 10%. Most wines fall from up to 150% to 30%. The formula stays the same; only the percentage shrinks.

steps.title: A quota caps the low rate
steps.text: A quota limits how many goods get the low rate each year. The deal reportedly allows 250,000 European vehicles a year. In a typical quota, goods beyond the cap pay the normal, higher rate.

example.setup: Imagine a European car that reaches India's border worth ₹20 lakh. Assume no other taxes or dealer margins, just the tariff.

example.result: Cutting the tariff from 110% to 10% removes ₹20 lakh of tax from a ₹20 lakh car, nearly halving its landed cost. But the cut comes gradually and only within the quota.

apply.text: This is what India gives up: border tax that kept European cars and wine costly. What it gets is the same formula working for its exporters. The EU cuts or removes tariffs on about 97% of its imports from India, and textile exporters stop paying 12–17%.

practice.q: Suppose a bottle of European wine reaches India's border worth ₹1,000. What is its landed cost at a 150% tariff, and at 30%?
practice.answer: At 150%: tax is 150% of ₹1,000 = ₹1,500, so landed cost is ₹1,000 + ₹1,500 = ₹2,500. At 30%: tax is ₹300, so landed cost is ₹1,300. The cut saves ₹1,200 per bottle, before other taxes and margins.

check.q: A European carmaker wants to send 300,000 cars a year to India at the deal's lowest tariff. What stands in its way?
options: The reported quota of 250,000 vehicles a year at the lower rate
The EU's carbon charge, CBAM
The EU's protection for sugar and rice
check.why: The low car tariff reportedly covers only 250,000 vehicles a year, and it falls to 10% gradually, not at once.

takeaways: A tariff is a percentage tax on an import's border value; trade deals cut the rate.
India cuts duties on EU cars and wine; the EU cuts tariffs on about 97% of Indian goods.
Watch the likely 16 December signing, then European Parliament consent before the 2027 start.

stories.headline: Nvidia faces SEC accounting probe as the AI stock rout deepens
stories.question: Is the AI stock boom breaking, and what happens when Wall Street reopens on 23 November?
stories.dek: Nvidia now faces a reported SEC look at its accounting after tech's worst week since 2020. Payoff doubts and rate-hike bets drove the fall; no source forecasts the 23 November open.

so_far.text: In November 2026 Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned after revelations about affairs, including one with a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence suspects of working for Beijing. Colette Kress became interim CEO. On 19 November Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI, listed on Nasdaq at $83 a share. It raised about $81.3bn, the largest IPO (first public sale of shares) on record, and closed that day at $97.17. On 20 November the S&P 500 and the Dow entered a correction, at least 10% below recent highs, as investors doubted AI spending would pay off.

what_happened.text: The New York Times reported on 20–21 November that the SEC, America's stock market regulator, is examining Nvidia's accounting; the Wall Street Journal reported it first. People briefed said the inquiry is early and could end without charges, and its focus is unclear. On 20 November Nvidia fell 14%, and President Trump called for Huang's reinstatement; chairman Harvey Jones ruled it out. In the week to 20 November the Nasdaq fell 10.02%, the S&P 500 8.61% and the Dow 8.02%. CNBC called it tech's worst week since 2020.

steps.text: AI share prices assumed huge spending on chips and data centres would pay off later; investors began doubting that.
Fed minutes leaned toward higher rates, raising bets on a December hike; higher rates shrink the value of distant future profits.
Higher rates also squeeze borrowers: analyses say CoreWeave pays about 25% of revenue in interest, much of it variable-rate.
Nvidia, the boom's main chip supplier, led the tech sell-off; it lost its chief and faces a reported SEC inquiry.
The selling spread across AI stocks; the WSJ puts the AI wipeout on Wall Street at roughly $4 trillion.

history.text:
It began in November 2022, when OpenAI released ChatGPT and investors rushed into generative AI. Nvidia makes the chips that train these systems. In 2023 it passed a $1 trillion market value, and the first bubble warnings began.

In January 2025 came the first big scare. China's DeepSeek matched models built at far greater cost. Nvidia fell about 17% in a day, roughly $600bn, then recovered 8.8% the next day. The $500bn Stargate venture was founded the same month, so spending kept rising.

In 2025 Nvidia hit $4 trillion in July and $5 trillion in October, the first company to do so. In September it announced a $100bn investment in OpenAI, which would buy Nvidia chips. Critics called this circular financing: the same money going round in a loop. In October 2025 OpenAI struck deals with AMD and Oracle, the Oracle deal worth $300bn. The Bank of England warned of a possible sharp correction.

Then debt grew. Morgan Stanley estimated data-centre debt could exceed $1 trillion by 2028, and in 2026 the biggest cloud companies issued large long-dated bonds. In late June and July 2026 South Korea's KOSPI fell 44% in 40 days as returns on AI infrastructure lagged. On 8 October 2026 the cost of insuring Oracle's debt hit a record.

So by November 2026 prices were high, debts were large and investors were nervous. Huang's exit and Anthropic's IPO landed on top of that.

lesson.concept: How belief, not sales, can move a stock price
lesson.big_idea: A company's market value is its yearly sales times a multiple: how much investors pay per rupee of sales. When belief in future growth fades, the multiple shrinks and the price falls, even if sales don't.

steps.title: Market value is the price tag
steps.text: A company's market value is its share price times the number of shares. It is what the whole market says the company is worth at that moment.

steps.title: Compare value with yearly sales
steps.text: Divide market value by one year's sales to get the price-to-sales multiple. Anthropic trades at roughly 40 times sales, the Economic Times reports: investors pay about $40 for every $1 of yearly sales.

steps.title: A high multiple is a bet
steps.text: Nobody pays 40 years of sales for the business as it stands. A high multiple means investors expect sales, and later profits, to grow a lot.

steps.title: Doubts and rates shrink it
steps.text: If investors doubt that growth, the multiple falls. Higher interest rates also shrink the value of profits expected far in the future. In November, sources named both: doubts AI spending would pay off, and bets on a December Fed hike.

steps.title: Price follows the multiple
steps.text: Value equals multiple times sales. So when the multiple shrinks, the price falls straight away, even if sales have not changed at all.

Yearly sales rarely change in a day, so in the lesson's terms the multiple shrank. No source gives the exact reason; the Economic Times says the fall deepened concerns over stretched AI valuations.

practice.q: Same company, but its sales grow to ₹1,200 crore while the multiple still falls from 40 to 30. What is it worth after the change?
practice.answer: New value: 30 × ₹1,200 crore = ₹36,000 crore. Compared with ₹40,000 crore, that is ₹4,000 crore less. ₹4,000 ÷ ₹40,000 = 10%. Sales grew 20%, but the shrinking multiple still pulled the value down 10%.

stories.question: Why are central banks raising interest rates again, and what does that mean for India?
stories.dek: An oil shock has pushed inflation back up, so the Fed and the ECB are raising rates again. Higher US rates pull money towards the dollar, which puts pressure on the rupee and the RBI.

so_far.text: In late February 2026, US and Israeli strikes on Iran largely halted oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. A preliminary deal on 15 June aimed to end the fighting, but the energy shock continued. On 10 September the European Central Bank (ECB) raised rates. On 16 September the US Federal Reserve (the Fed) hiked for the first time in over three years. On 28 October the Fed held rates in a 10–2 vote. The two dissenters, Cook and Hammack, wanted a hike. By 16 October the RBI had raised rates for the first time in four years to defend the rupee.

what_happened.text: A report on 22 November said markets put over 90% odds on a Fed rate hike in December, even as President Donald Trump called for the world's lowest rates. On 17 November the CME FedWatch tool put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the 8–9 December meeting at about 95%, up from 77% in early November. US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October. On 22 November gold, copper and aluminium fell to at least seven-month lows. Gold is near a 14-month low.

history.text:
The US Federal Reserve was created on 23 December 1913, after a series of financial panics, notably the severe crisis of 1907. In 1979 Paul Volcker became Fed chair. Under him, the Fed's key rate peaked at 20% in June 1981. US inflation fell from 14.8% in March 1980 to below 3% by 1983. But a 1980–82 recession pushed unemployment above 10%. The lesson stayed: rate hikes can beat inflation, but they cost jobs.

The next big test came in 2021–23. Pandemic supply problems, large 2020–21 stimulus and the 2022 invasion of Ukraine raised energy and food prices. At least 75 central banks raised rates. The Fed began in March 2022 and peaked at 5.5% on 26 July 2023. The ECB reached 4% on 14 September 2023, its highest since the euro began in 1999. Rates later fell from those peaks. Then, in late February 2026, strikes on Iran started a new energy shock, and central banks turned back to hikes.

lesson.concept: How the real interest rate decides whether hikes work
lesson.big_idea: What matters is not the interest rate alone but the rate minus inflation, called the real rate. Only when it is clearly above zero does borrowing cost enough to cool prices.

steps.title: The key rate sets borrowing costs
steps.text: A central bank sets one key rate, the price of short-term money for banks. The Fed's range is now 3.75%–4.00%. Banks pass changes on to the rates on loans and deposits.

steps.title: Inflation shrinks what money buys
steps.text: Inflation is how fast prices rise. If prices rise 4% a year, you need ₹104 to buy what ₹100 bought last year. Fed officials projected 3.7% inflation for 2026.

steps.title: Real rate = rate minus inflation
steps.text: Subtract inflation from the interest rate. The answer, the real interest rate, shows how much richer a saver truly gets, or how much a borrower truly pays.

steps.title: Positive real rates cool spending
steps.text: When the real rate is above zero, saving pays and borrowing hurts. People and firms spend less, and price rises slow. When the real rate is near zero, a hike bites only a little.

example.setup: Say your bank pays 4% a year on a ₹1,00,000 deposit, and prices also rise 4% a year. Then the bank raises its rate to 6%.

lines.label: Interest earned
lines.note: Your deposit grows to ₹1,04,000.

lines.label: Price rise
lines.note: Inflation of 4% eats the same amount.

lines.label: Real rate
lines.note: You are no richer, so saving has no reward.

lines.label: Rate raised to 6%
lines.note: Now you gain ₹2,000 of extra buying power.

lines.label: Effect on borrowers
lines.note: People borrow and spend less, so prices cool.

example.result: A hike only bites when the rate beats inflation. Raising the rate from 4% to 6% turned a zero real rate into 2%, which rewards saving and discourages borrowing.

apply.text: The Fed's range is 3.75%–4.00%, and in September its officials projected 3.7% inflation for 2026. Subtract, and the real rate is close to zero. By the lesson's logic, that puts little brake on spending. Musalem of the St. Louis Fed expects several more hikes before spring 2027, and markets put about 95% odds on a December hike.

practice.q: Suppose a central bank's rate is 5% and inflation is 3%. What is the real rate? What if inflation jumps to 6% and the rate stays at 5%?
practice.answer: First case: 5% − 3% = 2%, a positive real rate. Second case: 5% − 6% = −1%. The real rate turns negative, so borrowing is effectively rewarded. The bank must raise its rate above 6% just to get back above zero.

scenes.say: Chaliye try karte hain. Maan lijiye aapka bank 1 lakh rupaye ke deposit par 4 percent deta hai. Aapko milte hain 4 hazaar rupaye. Lekin prices bhi 4 percent badhe. Jo saamaan 1 lakh ka tha, ab 1 lakh 4 hazaar ka hai.
scenes.speak: चलिए try करते हैं। मान लीजिए आपका bank 1 लाख रुपये के deposit पर 4 percent देता है। आपको मिलते हैं 4 हज़ार रुपये। लेकिन prices भी 4 percent बढ़े। जो सामान 1 लाख का था, अब 1 लाख 4 हज़ार का है।

scenes.say: Toh aapka real rate hai 4 minus 4, yaani zero. Aap ameer nahi hue. Ab bank rate badhakar 6 percent karta hai. 6 minus 4, matlab 2 percent real. Ab saving ka fayda hai, aur udhaar mehnga hai.
scenes.speak: तो आपका real rate है 4 minus 4, यानी zero। आप अमीर नहीं हुए। अब bank rate बढ़ाकर 6 percent करता है। 6 minus 4, मतलब 2 percent real। अब saving का फ़ायदा है, और उधार महँगा है।

scenes.say: Rates kahan jaane chahiye, is par raay alag alag hai. St. Louis Fed ke Musalem ko spring 2027 se pehle kai aur hikes ki ummeed hai. President Trump kehte hain US ko duniya ka sabse kam rate dena chahiye, 1 percent ya usse kam.
scenes.speak: Rates कहाँ जाने चाहिए, इस पर राय अलग अलग है। St. Louis Fed के Musalem को spring 2027 से पहले कई और hikes की उम्मीद है। President Trump कहते हैं US को दुनिया का सबसे कम rate देना चाहिए, 1 percent या उससे कम।

scenes.say: Aapke liye iska kya matlab? Ek aam myth hai ki US rates sirf Americans ke liye matter karte hain. Aisa nahi hai. Yeh rupee ko kamzor kar sakte hain, jisse oil jaise imports mehnge hote hain. Reserve Bank December mein half point hike par charcha kar sakta hai. SBI ko quarter point ki ummeed hai. Hikes se aam taur par floating rate loan ki EMI badhti hai.
scenes.show: Myth: US rates don't affect India
scenes.speak: आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब? एक आम myth है कि US rates सिर्फ़ Americans के लिए matter करते हैं। ऐसा नहीं है। ये rupee को कमज़ोर कर सकते हैं, जिससे oil जैसे imports महँगे होते हैं। Reserve Bank December में half point hike पर चर्चा कर सकता है। SBI को quarter point की उम्मीद है। Hikes से आम तौर पर floating rate loan की EMI बढ़ती है।

scenes.say: Ab seekh lagaiye. Fed ka rate lagbhag 4 percent hai. Uske officials ne 2026 ke liye lagbhag teen point saat percent inflation project kiya. Ghataiye, toh real rate zero ke kareeb hai. Matlab udhaar ki cost prices ke badhne se mushkil se zyada hai. Musalem ko spring 2027 se pehle kai aur hikes ki ummeed hai.
scenes.speak: अब सीख लगाइए। Fed का rate लगभग 4 percent है। उसके officials ने 2026 के लिए लगभग तीन point सात percent inflation project किया। घटाइए, तो real rate zero के करीब है। मतलब उधार की cost prices के बढ़ने से मुश्किल से ज़्यादा है। Musalem को spring 2027 से पहले कई और hikes की उम्मीद है।

scenes.say: Kya dekhna hai? Fed 8 aur 9 December ko faisla karega. ECB ki meeting 17 December ko hone ki ummeed hai. Abhi pata nahi: Reserve Bank kab faisla karega, kitna, uska exact current repo rate kya hai, aur kya Fed half point ka hike karega.
scenes.image: Marriner S. Eccles Federal Reserve Board Building
scenes.speak: क्या देखना है? Fed 8 और 9 December को फ़ैसला करेगा। ECB की meeting 17 December को होने की उम्मीद है। अभी पता नहीं: Reserve Bank कब फ़ैसला करेगा, कितना, उसका exact current repo rate क्या है, और क्या Fed half point का hike करेगा।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Hike tabhi asar karta hai jab rate inflation se aage ho: yahi real rate hai. Oil shock ne inflation wapas laaya, toh Fed aur ECB ne rates badhaye, aur rupee par dabaav aaya. Aur nazar rakhiye: Fed par 9 December ko, ECB par 17 December ko, aur India ke Reserve Bank par.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Hike तभी असर करता है जब rate inflation से आगे हो: यही real rate है। Oil shock ने inflation वापस लाया, तो Fed और ECB ने rates बढ़ाए, और rupee पर दबाव आया। और नज़र रखिए: Fed पर 9 December को, ECB पर 17 December को, और India के Reserve Bank पर।

stories.headline: Houthi missiles at Riyadh, Iranian strike in Bahrain stretch the Gulf war
stories.question: Is the Gulf war widening, with Houthi missiles at Riyadh and strikes in Bahrain?
stories.dek: On 21 November, attacks reached Riyadh, Bahrain and Hormuz shipping. Major combat is still largely paused and talks continue. So the war is spreading to more places, but at a low level.

so_far.text: In a notice on 13 November, Air India and Air India Express suspended Riyadh and Dammam flights until 30 November. About two days before 21 November, a Houthi strike damaged Riyadh's PIF tower. After coalition strikes on Hodeidah port, the Houthis threatened Jeddah, other Red Sea ports, Riyadh's financial centre and the Al-Shuqaiq power station. On 19 November, Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met senior Qatari officials in Berlin about mediation. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says messages still pass between Tehran and Washington through mediators.

what_happened.text: Early on 21 November, the Saudi-led coalition intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh. No damage or casualties were reported. It was Riyadh's third straight day of emergency alerts, with eight in 24 hours. The same day, Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire but no injuries. Smoke rose over Sitra Island, home to a Bapco refinery. Iran's IRGC said it fired at US positions at Al-Riffa and Awali bases. Two tankers leaving the Gulf were struck: UKMTO says by projectiles, Iran's army says by a mine. Trump told Fox News he wants a 'permanent' Iran deal.

steps.text: Coalition strikes on Hodeidah port drew Houthi threats against Jeddah, Riyadh's financial centre and the Al-Shuqaiq power station.
Even missiles that get shot down keep Riyadh under repeated alerts, so the Houthis apply pressure without needing to cause damage.
Iran's IRGC says it targeted US positions in Bahrain; Bahrain says an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility.
Yet major combat has largely halted since April, and Trump has indicated large-scale attacks would resume only after January.
So the war spreads to more places at a low level, while indirect talks continue through mediators.

history.text:
The roots go back to 2015, when a nuclear deal with Iran known as the JCPOA was signed. In 2018 the US withdrew from it, removing the main agreement that had managed the nuclear dispute. In June 2025 came the Twelve-Day War, and in September 2025 UN 'snapback' sanctions returned.

On 28 February 2026 the US-Israeli war on Iran began. Strikes killed Supreme Leader Khamenei. Iran then blocked the Strait of Hormuz, causing a global fuel crisis. A nuclear dispute had become an energy shock for the whole world.

A ceasefire began on 8 April. Talks in Islamabad failed on 12–13 April, and the US blockaded Iran. An indefinite ceasefire followed on 21 April, then a memorandum on 17 June. That memorandum collapsed on 8 July after Iran hit ships in Hormuz. Even so, Reuters and AFP report that major combat has largely halted since the April ceasefire, while lower-level fighting continues.

A second front opened in Yemen. From September 2026 the Houthis escalated Yemen's civil war. In October they attacked Saudi airports with drones and missiles. That put Saudi Arabia directly in the line of fire and set the stage for the missiles aimed at Riyadh in November.

lesson.concept: Why war headlines don't always lift oil prices
lesson.big_idea: An oil price reflects the barrels actually reaching buyers plus a fear premium for barrels that might be lost. If tankers keep sailing, attacks raise fear but not shortage, so prices move little.

steps.title: Price follows barrels and buyers
steps.text: Brent is the main world benchmark price for crude oil. When fewer barrels reach buyers than they want, buyers bid the price up. When barrels flow freely, the price settles.

steps.title: Add a fear premium
steps.text: Traders also pay extra for the risk that supply could be cut in the coming weeks. This extra is the fear premium; economists call it a risk premium. It rises with threats and shrinks when nothing actually stops.

steps.title: Check whether barrels really stop
steps.text: After the war began on 28 February 2026, Iran blocked Hormuz and a global fuel crisis followed: real barrels were lost. By late November, Hormuz flows had recovered close to pre-war levels, limiting price moves.

steps.title: Turn the price into a bill
steps.text: About 52% of India's crude imports pass through Hormuz. Each $10 rise in crude adds roughly $13–14 billion to India's yearly import bill. A $10 fall saves roughly the same.

example.setup: Suppose oil would cost $80 a barrel with no war fears. Attacks add a $15 fear premium. Then tankers keep sailing through Hormuz, and the premium shrinks to $5.

apply.text: In the week to 20 November, a Houthi strike damaged Riyadh's PIF tower and alerts sounded. Yet one report says Brent fell 3.4%, its third weekly fall, because Hormuz flows were near pre-war levels. The fear premium stayed small. If attacks like the 21 November tanker strikes ever stopped real barrels, India would pay about $13–14 billion more a year for each $10 rise.

practice.q: Suppose attacks do stop tankers and Brent jumps from $90 to $110. Roughly how much more would India pay for oil in a year?
practice.answer: Rise = $110 − $90 = $20. That is two lots of $10. Each $10 adds about $13–14 billion. So 2 × $13–14 billion = about $26–28 billion more a year.

stories.headline: Russian ships hit by drones off Finland and in Libya
stories.question: Is Ukraine taking its drone war to Russian ships far from the front?
stories.dek: Within two days, drones hit a Russian cargo ship near Finland and a Russian warship in Libya, which reportedly sank. Finland's military says Ukraine likely hit the first. Nobody has claimed the second.

so_far.text: Ukraine has hit Russian ships with naval drones (small unmanned boats packed with explosives) since at least 2023. Finland's military said that in the week before the Sparta II attack, it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area of the Gulf of Finland. Ukraine's SBU security service named that ship as the corvette Naro-Fominsk. It said the ship was attacked on 11 November during a drone raid on the Ust-Luga oil depot. Separately, on 20 November Russia struck Kyiv with more than 400 drones and 110 missiles, according to President Zelensky.

what_happened.text: Early on 22 November, a Russian warship docked at Benghazi, Libya, was struck in a suspected Ukrainian sea-drone attack. The corvette Merkury reportedly capsized and sank; only its bow stayed above water. Reports say several people died and at least 10 were injured. Libya's eastern government said the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia. On 21 November, two drones hit the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland. It caught fire and drifted into Finnish waters. All 16 crew were evacuated. Ukraine has not confirmed the Benghazi strike.

steps.text: Since 2023, Ukraine has used naval drones, small unmanned boats with explosives, to hit Russian Black Sea Fleet ships.
Those strikes pushed Russia's Black Sea Fleet back from Crimea and switched it from attack to defence.
Russia still sends ships far from home: to Kaliningrad on the Baltic, and to eastern Libya, where it works with Haftar.
Suspected drone strikes now reach those ships far from the front, at sea near Finland and in port at Benghazi.
That pulls in other countries: Finland closed air and sea zones, and eastern Libya calls it an attack on its sovereignty.

history.text:
The sea war began near Ukraine. In April 2022 the Moskva, flagship of Russia's Black Sea Fleet, sank. Ukraine said two of its Neptune anti-ship missiles hit the ship. Russia said it sank under tow after an ammunition fire. It was the war's first big naval blow.

In July 2023 Ukraine used Sea Baby naval drones against the Kerch Strait Bridge to Crimea, damaging its road section. Its Magura V5 drone boats hit Black Sea Fleet ships, including the Ivanovets and the Caesar Kunikov. Small unmanned boats could now hit real warships.

The pressure worked. Ukrainian sea drones, missiles and aerial drones forced Russia to move part of the fleet from Crimea to Novorossiysk, and the fleet switched from attack to defence. In April 2024 a fire damaged the corvette Serpukhov at Baltiysk, in Russia's Kaliningrad region on the Baltic. Ukraine's GUR military intelligence later claimed it, an early sign of reach far from the front.

Russia's naval map was changing too. After Assad fell in Syria in December 2024, analysts said Russia might shift equipment and people to eastern Libya, where it works with Khalifa Haftar. That helps explain why a Russian warship was in Benghazi.

Ukraine then went after Russia's shadow-fleet tankers. On 28 November 2025 the SBU hit the tankers Kairos and Virat in the Black Sea off Turkey, using Sea Baby drones. On 19 December 2025 it said it hit the tanker Qendil in the Mediterranean with aerial drones, its first such strike outside the Black Sea.

lesson.concept: How drone swarms get past a warship's defences
lesson.big_idea: A warship can shoot down only some of the drones coming at it. If attackers send more than it can stop, a few get through, and a few hits can sink it.

steps.title: What a sea drone is
steps.text: A sea drone, or naval drone, is a small unmanned boat carrying explosives. An operator steers it remotely toward a ship. Ukraine has used types called Sea Baby and Magura V5 against Russian ships since 2023.

steps.title: Ships fire back
steps.text: A warship defends itself with guns, radar and lookouts. Each defence stops a share of the incoming drones, but never all of them. Think of that share as the crew's hit rate.

steps.title: Send many at once
steps.text: So attackers send many drones together, called a swarm. The defenders must stop every single one. The attacker needs only one or two to reach the ship's hull.

steps.title: Cheap drones, costly ships
steps.text: A drone costs far less than a warship. So the attacker can lose most of its drones and still come out ahead if two of them strike.

steps.title: Reach far from home
steps.text: Drones can be launched close to a target, wherever it is. Libyan officials claim the drones that hit Merkury came from western Libya. Ukraine has not confirmed this.

example.setup: Imagine a Russian corvette docked in a foreign port. Assume its crew can stop 2 of every 3 drones that come at it. An attacker sends 6 drones together.

example.result: The crew stopped two-thirds of the drones and still took two hits. Spending ₹6 crore to threaten a ₹500 crore ship is a trade that favours the attacker.

apply.text: This is the pattern Libyan military officials described to AP at Benghazi: at least four drones intercepted and two that struck the Merkury, which reportedly sank. Ukraine has not confirmed this. Off Finland, two drones hit the Sparta II. A ship docked or sailing far from the front is now a target.

practice.q: Suppose the crew improves and stops 3 of every 4 drones. The attacker sends 8. How many hit? How many must it send for 3 hits?
practice.answer: Stopped: 8 × 3/4 = 6. Hits: 8 − 6 = 2. Now 1 in every 4 gets through, so 3 hits need 3 × 4 = 12 drones. Better defence just means the attacker sends more.

scenes.say: Yahan tak pahunche kaise? April 2022 mein Russia ki Black Sea Fleet ka flagship, Moskva, doob gaya. Ukraine ne kaha do Neptune missiles ne use hit kiya. Russia ne ship par lagi aag ko zimmedar bataya. Yeh is war ka pehla bada naval jhatka tha.
scenes.speak: यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? April 2022 में Russia की Black Sea Fleet का flagship, Moskva, डूब गया। Ukraine ने कहा दो Neptune missiles ने उसे hit किया। Russia ने ship पर लगी आग को ज़िम्मेदार बताया। यह इस war का पहला बड़ा naval झटका था।

scenes.say: July 2023 mein Ukraine ke Sea Baby drones ne, yaani explosives se bhari chhoti unmanned boats ne, Crimea jaane wale Kerch Strait Bridge ko nuksaan pahunchaya. Magura drone boats ne Caesar Kunikov jaise warships ko hit kiya. Russia ko apni fleet ka ek hissa Crimea se Novorossiysk le jaana pada, aur defence par aana pada.
scenes.show: Drone boats push the fleet back
scenes.speak: July 2023 में Ukraine के Sea Baby drones ने, यानी explosives से भरी छोटी unmanned boats ने, Crimea जाने वाले Kerch Strait Bridge को नुकसान पहुँचाया। Magura drone boats ने Caesar Kunikov जैसे warships को hit किया। Russia को अपनी fleet का एक हिस्सा Crimea से Novorossiysk ले जाना पड़ा, और defence पर आना पड़ा।

scenes.say: Phir pahunch badhti gayi. April 2024 mein Baltic par Kaliningrad mein ek aag ne Russian corvette ko nuksaan pahunchaya. Baad mein Ukraine ki military intelligence ne iski zimmedari li. December 2024 mein Syria mein Assad ke girne ke baad analysts ne kaha ki Russia apne assets eastern Libya shift kar sakta hai, jahan woh Khalifa Haftar ke saath kaam karta hai. Benghazi ki kahani yahin se samajh aati hai.
scenes.speak: फिर पहुँच बढ़ती गई। April 2024 में Baltic पर Kaliningrad में एक आग ने Russian corvette को नुकसान पहुँचाया। बाद में Ukraine की military intelligence ने इसकी ज़िम्मेदारी ली। December 2024 में Syria में Assad के गिरने के बाद analysts ने कहा कि Russia अपने assets eastern Libya shift कर सकता है, जहाँ वो Khalifa Haftar के साथ काम करता है। Benghazi की कहानी यहीं से समझ आती है।

Black Sea ke bahar yeh uska aisa pehla strike tha.
scenes.show: Tankers hit: Black Sea, then Mediterranean
scenes.speak: उसके बाद आया shadow fleet, यानी Russian oil ले जाने वाले tankers। 28 November 2025 को Ukraine की SBU security service ने Sea Baby drones से Turkey के पास दो tankers को hit किया। 19 December 2025 को SBU ने कहा कि aerial drones ने Mediterranean में एक tanker को hit किया। Black Sea के बाहर यह उसका ऐसा पहला strike था।

scenes.say: Sparta Two attack se pehle wale hafte mein, Finland ki military ne kaha ki use Gulf ke usi hisse mein ek Russian warship par strike ka pata chala tha. Ukraine ki SBU ne bataya ki yeh corvette Naro-Fominsk tha, jise 11 November ko Ust-Luga oil depot par drone raid mein hit kiya gaya.
scenes.speak: Sparta Two attack से पहले वाले हफ़्ते में, Finland की military ने कहा कि उसे Gulf के उसी हिस्से में एक Russian warship पर strike का पता चला था। Ukraine की SBU ने बताया कि यह corvette Naro-Fominsk था, जिसे 11 November को Ust-Luga oil depot पर drone raid में hit किया गया।

scenes.say: Toh yeh sab ho kyon raha hai? Ek: 2023 se Ukraine Russian ships ke khilaf drone boats use kar raha hai. Do: isse Black Sea Fleet defence mein chali gayi. Teen: Russia ab bhi apne ships door bhejta hai, Kaliningrad aur eastern Libya tak. Chaar: ab suspected strikes unhe wahan bhi dhoondh lete hain. Paanch: isse Finland aur Libya bhi beech mein aa jaate hain.
scenes.show: Drones reach ships far from home
scenes.speak: तो यह सब हो क्यों रहा है? एक: 2023 से Ukraine Russian ships के ख़िलाफ़ drone boats use कर रहा है। दो: इससे Black Sea Fleet defence में चली गई। तीन: Russia अब भी अपने ships दूर भेजता है, Kaliningrad और eastern Libya तक। चार: अब suspected strikes उन्हें वहाँ भी ढूँढ लेते हैं। पाँच: इससे Finland और Libya भी बीच में आ जाते हैं।

scenes.say: Ek dukaandaar socho, jo chori ke baad apna maal peeche ke godaam mein shift kar deta hai. Ab chor uski delivery vans ko door jaakar hit karta hai, tab bhi jab woh doosron ke pumps par fuel bharwa rahi hoti hain. Lekin yeh misaal yahan tootti hai: yeh do deshon ke beech ki war hai, aur Libya kehta hai ki woh isme shaamil nahi hai.
scenes.show: Hit far from home, even refuelling
scenes.speak: एक दुकानदार सोचो, जो चोरी के बाद अपना माल पीछे के गोदाम में shift कर देता है। अब चोर उसकी delivery vans को दूर जाकर hit करता है, तब भी जब वो दूसरों के pumps पर fuel भरवा रही होती हैं। लेकिन यह मिसाल यहाँ टूटती है: यह दो देशों के बीच की war है, और Libya कहता है कि वो इसमें शामिल नहीं है।

scenes.say: Ab idea: drone swarms ek warship ki defence ko kaise paar karte hain. Step one: sea drone ek chhoti unmanned boat hai, explosives se bhari, jise door se chalaya jaata hai. Step two: warship guns, radar aur lookouts se jawab deta hai. Woh kuch drones rokta hai, sab kabhi nahi.
scenes.speak: अब idea: drone swarms एक warship की defence को कैसे पार करते हैं। Step one: sea drone एक छोटी unmanned boat है, explosives से भरी, जिसे दूर से चलाया जाता है। Step two: warship guns, radar और lookouts से जवाब देता है। वो कुछ drones रोकता है, सब कभी नहीं।

scenes.say: Step three: isliye attackers ek saath bahut saare bhejte hain, yaani swarm. Defenders ko har ek rokna padta hai, attacker ko bas ek ya do hits chahiye. Step four: drones warships se bahut saste hain, toh zyada tar kho dena bhi chalta hai. Step five: drones target ke paas se launch ho sakte hain, target jahan bhi ho.
scenes.speak: Step three: इसलिए attackers एक साथ बहुत सारे भेजते हैं, यानी swarm। Defenders को हर एक रोकना पड़ता है, attacker को बस एक या दो hits चाहिए। Step four: drones warships से बहुत सस्ते हैं, तो ज़्यादा तर खो देना भी चलता है। Step five: drones target के पास से launch हो सकते हैं, target जहाँ भी हो।

scenes.say: Maan lijiye ek corvette hai, jiska crew har 3 mein se 2 drones rok leta hai. Yeh rate assumed hai. 6 drones ek saath aate hain. 6 ka do-tihai hai 4, toh 4 maar giraye gaye. 6 mein se 4 gaye, bache 2 hits. Ek drone 1 crore rupaye ka maan lein, toh kharch hua 6 crore. Aur saamne ship, maan lijiye 500 crore ka.
scenes.speak: मान लीजिए एक corvette है, जिसका crew हर 3 में से 2 drones रोक लेता है। यह rate assumed है। 6 drones एक साथ आते हैं। 6 का दो-तिहाई है 4, तो 4 मार गिराए गए। 6 में से 4 गए, बचे 2 hits। एक drone 1 करोड़ रुपये का मान लें, तो ख़र्च हुआ 6 करोड़। और सामने ship, मान लीजिए 500 करोड़ का।

scenes.say: Toh crew ne zyada tar drones roke, phir bhi haar gaya. Ab khud try kijiye: crew ab har 4 mein se 3 rokta hai, aur 8 drones aate hain. 6 ruk gaye, toh 2 phir bhi hit karte hain. 3 hits chahiye? 12 bhejiye. Better defence ka matlab bas zyada drones.

scenes.say: Kaun kya keh raha hai? Finland ke Prime Minister Orpo kehte hain ki war phail rahi hai, aur Ukraine ko aggressor se ladne ka haq hai. Finland ki military kehti hai ki shayad Ukraine ne Sparta Two ko hit kiya. Libya ki eastern government Benghazi ko apni sovereignty par hamla bataati hai. Tripoli ki government Libyan waters ko proxy war ke liye use karne ko condemn karti hai.

Finland के Prime Minister Orpo कहते हैं कि war फैल रही है, और Ukraine को aggressor से लड़ने का हक़ है। Finland की military कहती है कि शायद Ukraine ने Sparta Two को hit किया। Libya की eastern government Benghazi को अपनी sovereignty पर हमला बताती है। Tripoli की government Libyan waters को proxy war के लिए use करने को condemn करती है।

Estonia ke navy chief, Ivo Vark, kehte hain ki Gulf mein aur attacks se inkaar nahi kiya ja sakta. Jo ab bhi pata nahi: Benghazi mein kitne log maare gaye, aur Sparta Two mein cargo kya tha.

thread.previously: The US is tightening routes Chinese firms use to reach advanced chips. A BIS rule issued 16 November 2026, reported effective 19 November, requires data-centre licences in five countries, restricts remote access and ends a foundry self-certification exemption. TSMC and Samsung paused some China shipments pending licences. California's AG subpoenaed Nvidia on 19 November; Nvidia fell 3.3%. Malaysia is seen as most exposed. India is not named.
thread.changed: On 22 November Jay Clayton said China likely found channels to Nvidia's top chips and confirmed a probe of Alice Huang and Megaspeed. Nvidia halted Hopper shipments to China; Huang faces House committees on 1 December.

stories.headline: US intelligence chief says China found ways to get Nvidia chips
stories.question: How is China getting banned Nvidia AI chips, and what is the US doing about it?
stories.dek: US officials point to middlemen abroad, smuggling cases and possibly China's spy agency. Washington is answering with investigations, new licence rules and questions for Nvidia's leaders.

so_far.text: On 16 November 2026 the US export regulator, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), issued a rule requiring licences for advanced chip shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Data centres anywhere that serve China-headquartered firms above a size limit also need licences. Around 12 November, Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang left after admitting an affair, while denying wrongdoing. California's Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China and misled investors.

what_happened.text: On 22 November 2026, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN he expects China has found channels to obtain Nvidia's top AI chips. He pointed to a New York federal indictment over diversion efforts. On ABC he called Nvidia chips "the jewel" and confirmed a US investigation into Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, and her company. Earlier reports, still unconfirmed, allege China's Ministry of State Security recruited her. The New York Times, citing officials, reported that China's spy agency has run a years-long campaign to help Chinese firms get advanced chips. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing; no charges have been filed.

steps.text: US rules block the top chips from going straight to China, so demand shifts to middlemen in other countries.
Firms in places like Singapore and Malaysia can buy chips legally, then pass them on or rent their computing to Chinese customers.
As of 12 November, renting chips abroad to Chinese firms like Alibaba broke no US rule, because the chips never entered China.
US officials also say China's spy agency has helped Chinese firms get chips and gathered intelligence on the industry.
So the US now targets the middle: licences for five transit countries and for large data centres serving Chinese firms.

history.text:
It began in 2022, when the Biden administration built a wide system of export controls on AI chips. An export control means a product needs a US licence, or permission, before going to certain places. A 2025 Biden-era framework sorted countries into tiers. India was in the second tier, so Indian firms could import top chips only with licences, in limited amounts.

In 2025 the Trump administration reversed the AI Diffusion Rule. A draft rule aimed at Malaysia and Thailand was never issued.

Direct sales to China also widened. A House committee says nearly 880,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD chips were approved for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026. In 2026, H200 chip sales to China were allowed case by case, with the US taking a 25% cut.

Then the gaps showed. In January 2026 the Remote Access Security Act passed the House 369–22 but stalled in the Senate. In March 2026, US charges against a Super Micro executive and two others alleged that $2.5bn of Nvidia servers were diverted to China.

In November 2026 events sped up. Jensen Huang left Nvidia around 12 November. BIS issued its licence rule on 16 November. On 17 November Nvidia created a board-level export-control oversight committee. Acting CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia would stop shipping Hopper data-centre chips to China.

analogy.text: Think of a shop that may not sell to one customer. The customer sends a friend to buy instead, or pays to use the goods at the friend's home. The US is now checking the friends: licences for buyers in nearby countries and for homes that rent to the banned customer.
analogy.breaks: Goods at a home must be used there, but computing power can be used from across the world over the internet.

for_you.text: India is not one of the five countries in the rule, so chip shipments to India are not newly licensed. But the data-centre clause applies anywhere: an Indian operator serving China-headquartered firms above the size limit would need a US licence. India was in the second tier of the 2025 framework, and a February 2026 India–US interim trade deal aims to widen GPU access.

misconception.myth: China can get banned chips only by smuggling them across borders.
misconception.fact: Renting is another route. As of 12 November, renting chips in foreign data centres to Chinese firms like Alibaba broke no US rule. The 16 November rule now requires licences above a size limit.

lesson.concept: How chips reach China around US export controls
lesson.big_idea: Export controls stop direct sales, so demand flows through middlemen who resell chips or rent out their computing. The US closes these routes by requiring licences at each middle stop.

steps.title: Start with a licence
steps.text: An export control says a product needs US permission, a licence, before going to certain buyers. The US built a wide system of these controls on AI chips in 2022.

steps.title: Route one: resell abroad
steps.text: A firm in another country buys chips legally, then passes them on to China. US charges in March 2026 alleged $2.5bn of Nvidia servers moved this way.

steps.title: Route two: rent, don't ship
steps.text: A data centre abroad keeps the chips and rents their computing over the internet. As of 12 November, renting to Chinese firms like Alibaba broke no US rule.

steps.title: Measure the data centre
steps.text: Each chip has a computing score called TPP, total processing performance. Add up the scores of all the chips and you get the centre's aggregate, or total, TPP.

practice.q: A data centre in Brazil has 1,000 chips, assume 10,000 TPP each, and serves only Chinese firms. Does the data-centre clause require a licence?
practice.answer: Total: 1,000 × 10,000 = 10 million TPP. That is below the 12 million limit, so the data-centre clause does not apply. But Brazil is one of the five countries, so new chip shipments to it still need licences.

stories.headline: Arunachal villagers reject Amit Shah's offer of talks on Siang dam
stories.question: Why are Arunachal villagers resisting India's biggest dam despite Amit Shah's offer of talks?
stories.dek: Adi groups want no dam and the survey stopped. They refuse talks while security forces stay and police cases remain. The Centre calls it a national project and a buffer against China.

so_far.text: The Siang river enters Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet, where it is called the Yarlung Tsangpo. NHPC, the state-run hydropower company, plans the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project on it. It would be India's biggest dam. The project is still at the survey stage, and villagers have blocked drilling at three sites. Residents say paramilitary personnel are deployed in Upper Siang villages. In a report dated 6 November 2026, the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF) refused the Arunachal government's call for talks until arrests stopped and central forces left.

what_happened.text: On 20 November 2026, two Adi bodies gave Home Minister Amit Shah a memorandum. They were Adi Ba:né Kébang United, the apex Adi council, and SIFF. They demanded no dam on the Siang and a halt to the pre-feasibility survey. On 21 November, Shah said 'positive and constructive' talks would be held with stakeholders. He called the dam a national project, vital for Arunachal's development, energy security and strategic interests. NDTV reported on 22 November that an anti-dam group in Siang Valley rejected the offer. It said talks cannot proceed while security forces stay deployed and cases against protesters remain.

steps.text: China began building a dam of about 60,000 MW upstream, so Delhi wants its own dam downstream as a buffer.
In general, any dam stores water in a lake behind it, and in a valley that lake can cover homes and farms.
The Adi groups demand that the pre-feasibility survey be suspended, and villagers have blocked drilling at three sites.
The groups point to arrests, at least 40 police cases and paramilitary troops in villages as reasons to refuse talks.
So the groups set conditions first: withdraw forces and drop cases, and only then talk.

history.text: Adi villagers along the Siang have protested against dam plans since 2008-09. In 2017, NITI Aayog, the government's policy think tank, proposed a giant dam on the Siang. Its stated aim was to counter Chinese hydropower projects upstream on the Yarlung Tsangpo. That turned a local power project into a matter of national strategy. In April 2022, the Centre directed NHPC to carry out a pre-feasibility survey, a first study of whether a site can work. NHPC chose three sites: Uggeng, Ditte Dimme and Parong. The threat became concrete for villagers. Parong's headman said 43 of its 116 families would have their homes submerged. On 19 July 2025, China's Premier Li Qiang inaugurated construction of the Medog dam on the lower Yarlung Tsangpo, estimated at about 60,000 MW. Indian officials say the Siang dam would act as a buffer and flood cushion against sudden releases from it. That raised the stakes for Delhi. Tension on the ground grew too. Lawyers and activists say at least 40 FIRs (police cases) have been filed against protesters since 2025. On 23 October 2026, a protest in Pasighat turned violent after tear gas was fired. An NHPC office and a police station were set on fire, and police arrested 69 people.

lesson.concept: How a dam's lake works as a flood cushion
lesson.big_idea: A dam can soak up a sudden surge of water only if its lake has room to rise. More room means a bigger lake, and a bigger lake covers more land.

steps.title: A dam makes a lake
steps.text: A dam is a wall across a river. Water piles up behind it into a lake, called a reservoir. The wall's height and the valley's shape decide how far the water spreads.

steps.title: Empty space is the cushion
steps.text: A 'flood cushion' is space in the lake kept empty on purpose. If extra water rushes in, the lake rises into that space instead of flooding towns below. Indian officials say the Siang dam would play this role against sudden releases from China's Medog dam.

steps.title: Room equals area times rise
steps.text: The water a lake can soak up is roughly its surface area multiplied by how far it can rise. A small lake must rise a lot to hold a surge. A wide lake rises only a little.

steps.title: Bigger cushion, more land underwater
steps.text: To catch a bigger surge safely, a dam needs a wider or deeper lake. Either way, more valley land usually goes under water. That is the general trade-off any flood-cushion dam faces.

example.setup: Imagine a sudden release upstream sends 10 crore cubic metres of extra water towards a valley. A dam downstream wants to catch all of it. Assume its lake covers 10 square km.

lines.label: Lake area in metres
lines.note: One square km is 10 lakh square metres.

lines.label: How far it rises
lines.note: Water volume divided by surface area gives the rise.

lines.label: Safe rise
lines.calc: Assume the lake can safely rise only 5 metres
lines.note: Any higher and the dam could overflow or be damaged.

lines.label: Area needed instead
lines.calc: 10 crore ÷ 5 = 2 crore sq m = 20 sq km
lines.note: Halve the rise, and the lake must double in area.

example.result: The lake catches the whole surge, so towns below stay safe. But to stay within a safe rise, the lake had to double from 10 to 20 square km. In a lived-in valley, that extra land is where people are.

apply.text: Indian officials want the Siang dam as a buffer against sudden releases from China's Medog dam, begun on 19 July 2025. Our example shows the general trade-off: more cushion usually means a bigger lake. How big the Siang lake would be is not known. Separately, SIFF estimates 27 villages would be affected, and Parong's headman said 43 of 116 families would have homes submerged.

practice.q: Same surge of 10 crore cubic metres, but now the lake covers 25 square km. How far does the lake rise?
practice.answer: First convert the area: 25 sq km = 2.5 crore square metres. Then divide volume by area: 10 crore ÷ 2.5 crore = 4 metres. The wider lake rises less, but it now covers 25 square km of land.

check.q: In general, why does a dam with a bigger flood cushion tend to put more land under water?

check.why: Water a lake can soak up is roughly area times rise. If the safe rise is limited, more water needs more area.

scenes.speak: 20 November 2026 को, Adi community के दो groups ने Amit Shah को एक memorandum दिया। Adi, Siang valley की एक indigenous community है। उनकी माँग: Siang पर कोई dam नहीं, और शुरुआती survey बंद करो।

Group ka kehna tha, jab tak security forces wahan hain aur protesters par cases chal rahe hain, tab tak koi baatcheet nahi.

Adi gaon wale 2008 ya 9 se Siang par dam plans ka virodh kar rahe hain. 2017 mein NITI Aayog, yaani sarkar ke think tank, ne yahan ek giant dam ka proposal diya. scenes.speak: तो यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? Adi गाँव वाले 2008 या 9 से Siang पर dam plans का विरोध कर रहे हैं। 2017 में NITI Aayog, यानी सरकार के think tank, ने यहाँ एक giant dam का proposal दिया। मकसद था upstream China के hydropower projects का जवाब देना, जहाँ इस river को Yarlung Tsangpo कहते हैं।

Matlab pehli study ki koi site chal sakti hai ya nahi. Teen sites chuni gayi: Uggeng, Ditte Dimme aur Parong. Parong ke headman ne kaha ki 116 mein se 43 parivaron ke ghar paani mein doob jayenge.
scenes.speak: इससे एक local power project national strategy बन गया। April 2022 में Centre ने NHPC, यानी सरकारी hydropower company, को pre-feasibility survey करने को कहा। मतलब पहली study कि कोई site चल सकती है या नहीं। तीन sites चुनी गईं: Uggeng, Ditte Dimme और Parong। Parong के headman ने कहा कि 116 में से 43 परिवारों के घर पानी में डूब जाएँगे।

scenes.speak: फिर China ने कदम उठाया। 19 July 2025 को Premier Li Qiang ने upstream Medog dam का construction शुरू किया। Indian officials कहते हैं कि Siang dam उसके अचानक छोड़े गए पानी के खिलाफ buffer और flood cushion का काम करेगा। इससे Delhi के लिए दाँव और बढ़ गया।

scenes.speak: Step three: Adi groups चाहते हैं कि survey suspend हो, और गाँव वालों ने तीन sites पर drilling रोक दी है। Step four: groups arrests, police cases और गाँव में troops को बातचीत ठुकराने की वजह बताते हैं। इसलिए उनकी शर्तें हैं: forces हटाओ, cases वापस लो, फिर बात करो।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jo sab jodta hai: dam ki lake flood cushion ka kaam kaise karti hai. Dam river ke aar paar khadi ek deewar hai. Uske peeche paani jama hokar lake ban jata hai. Flood cushion us lake mein khaali rakhi gayi jagah hai, taaki achanak aaye surge ko jaane ki jagah mile.
scenes.show: Flood cushion: empty space kept free
scenes.speak: अब वो एक idea जो सब जोड़ता है: dam की lake flood cushion का काम कैसे करती है। Dam river के आर पार खड़ी एक दीवार है। उसके पीछे पानी जमा होकर lake बन जाता है। Flood cushion उस lake में खाली रखी गई जगह है, ताकि अचानक आए surge को जाने की जगह मिले।

scenes.say: Lake kitna paani sokh sakti hai? Mote taur par, uska surface area guna woh kitna upar uth sakti hai. Chhoti lake ko kaafi upar uthna padta hai. Chaudi lake bas thoda sa uthti hai. Isliye bade surge ke liye aam taur par chaudi ya gehri lake chahiye, aur zyada zameen paani mein.
scenes.speak: Lake कितना पानी सोख सकती है? मोटे तौर पर, उसका surface area गुणा वो कितना ऊपर उठ सकती है। छोटी lake को काफ़ी ऊपर उठना पड़ता है। चौड़ी lake बस थोड़ा सा उठती है। इसलिए बड़े surge के लिए आम तौर पर चौड़ी या गहरी lake चाहिए, और ज़्यादा ज़मीन पानी में।

scenes.say: Ek example dekhte hain. Maan lijiye 10 crore cubic metre paani ka surge aata hai. Lake 10 square kilometre mein faili hai, yaani 1 crore square metre. Paani ko area se divide kijiye: 10 crore bata 1 crore. Lake 10 metre upar uthti hai.
scenes.speak: एक example देखते हैं। मान लीजिए 10 करोड़ cubic metre पानी का surge आता है। Lake 10 square kilometre में फैली है, यानी 1 करोड़ square metre। पानी को area से divide कीजिए: 10 करोड़ बटा 1 करोड़। Lake 10 metre ऊपर उठती है।

scenes.say: Ab maan lijiye lake safely sirf 5 metre uth sakti hai. 10 crore bata 5 hua 2 crore square metre. Yaani 20 square kilometre, toh lake double ho jaati hai. Neeche ke shehar safe rehte hain, lekin basi hui valley mein woh extra zameen wahi hai jahan log rehte hain.
scenes.show: Halve the rise, double the lake
scenes.speak: अब मान लीजिए lake safely सिर्फ़ 5 metre उठ सकती है। 10 करोड़ बटा 5 हुआ 2 करोड़ square metre। यानी 20 square kilometre, तो lake double हो जाती है। नीचे के शहर safe रहते हैं, लेकिन बसी हुई valley में वो extra ज़मीन वही है जहाँ लोग रहते हैं।

scenes.say: Toh kaun kya keh raha hai? Amit Shah kehte hain yeh national project hai, aur Centre baatcheet se logon ko bharose mein lega. Adi groups kehte hain koi dam nahi, survey suspend karo, aur forces aur cases ke saaye mein koi baatcheet nahi. Pema Khandu vaada karte hain ki koi zabardasti displacement nahi hoga, aur public consultation ke bina koi faisla nahi.
scenes.speak: तो कौन क्या कह रहा है? Amit Shah कहते हैं यह national project है, और Centre बातचीत से लोगों को भरोसे में लेगा। Adi groups कहते हैं कोई dam नहीं, survey suspend करो, और forces और cases के साये में कोई बातचीत नहीं। Pema Khandu वादा करते हैं कि कोई ज़बरदस्ती displacement नहीं होगा, और public consultation के बिना कोई फ़ैसला नहीं।

scenes.speak: आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? अभी आपके bills में कुछ नहीं बदलता। Project अभी सिर्फ़ pre-feasibility survey stage पर है। और survey approval नहीं होता। Pema Khandu कहते हैं कि public consultation के बिना कोई फ़ैसला नहीं लिया जाएगा।

scenes.say: Ab sabak lagaiye. Delhi China ke Medog dam ke khilaf cushion ke roop mein Siang dam chahta hai. Aam taur par, zyada cushion ka matlab badi lake. Siang ki lake kitni badi hogi, yeh pata nahi hai. India ke saamne yahi mushkil choice hai: ek taraf security aur energy, doosri taraf logon ki zameen.
scenes.speak: अब सबक लगाइए। Delhi China के Medog dam के खिलाफ cushion के रूप में Siang dam चाहता है। आम तौर पर, ज़्यादा cushion का मतलब बड़ी lake। Siang की lake कितनी बड़ी होगी, यह पता नहीं है। India के सामने यही मुश्किल choice है: एक तरफ़ security और energy, दूसरी तरफ़ लोगों की ज़मीन।

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? Baatcheet ki koi date ya format announce nahi hua hai. Dekhiye ki forces hatti hain ya cases wapas hote hain, aur survey aur drilling phir shuru hoti hai ya nahi. Abhi bhi pata nahi: kitne log affect honge, dam ka exact size, aur kitne troops tainaat hain.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? बातचीत की कोई date या format announce नहीं हुआ है। देखिए कि forces हटती हैं या cases वापस होते हैं, और survey और drilling फिर शुरू होती है या नहीं। अभी भी पता नहीं: कितने लोग affect होंगे, dam का exact size, और कितने troops तैनात हैं।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Dam ki lake surge ko tabhi rok paati hai jab usmein khaali jagah ho, aur jagah ka matlab aam taur par doobi hui zameen. Adi groups ne Shah ka offer thukra diya, woh chahte hain forces hatein, cases wapas hon aur koi dam na bane. Aur dekhte rahiye, baatcheet ki date aati hai ya nahi, aur survey phir shuru hota hai ya nahi.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Dam की lake surge को तभी रोक पाती है जब उसमें खाली जगह हो, और जगह का मतलब आम तौर पर डूबी हुई ज़मीन। Adi groups ने Shah का offer ठुकरा दिया, वो चाहते हैं forces हटें, cases वापस हों और कोई dam न बने। और देखते रहिए, बातचीत की date आती है या नहीं, और survey फिर शुरू होता है या नहीं।

stories.headline: India's common antibiotics are losing power, ICMR data shows
stories.question: Which common antibiotics are failing in India, and what does that mean for patients?
stories.dek: ICMR data shows key antibiotics now stop far fewer common infections than in 2017. That includes powerful reserve drugs. Doctors' first choices fail more often, and fewer backup options remain.

so_far.text: Antibiotics kill bacteria. But bacteria can change so that a drug no longer works. This is called antimicrobial resistance, or AMR. ICMR, the Indian Council of Medical Research, runs a national AMR Surveillance Network. The network tests bacteria taken from patients and publishes a report every year. Its report covering 2023 found steep falls since 2017 in how often common drugs stopped E. coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Its 2024 report, the eighth edition, found these two were the bacteria most often found in samples.

what_happened.text: On 22 November 2026, The Times of India reported that ICMR says common antibiotics are losing potency as drug resistance rises. It is not yet clear which ICMR report the article is based on. ICMR's data covering 2023 shows the pattern. E. coli susceptibility to piperacillin-tazobactam fell from 56.8% in 2017 to 42.4% in 2023. Klebsiella susceptibility to imipenem, a reserve drug, fell from 58.5% to 35.6%. Over 95% of typhoid bacteria resisted fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin. One bright spot: in 2024, E. coli susceptibility to ceftazidime rose from 19.2% to 27.5%.

steps.text: Every antibiotic dose kills the bacteria it can, so any resistant ones survive and multiply.
Easy over-the-counter sales and heavy hospital use give resistant bacteria many such chances; Schedule H1 enforcement has been weak.
Farms add pressure: a CSE study found 27 critically important antibiotics used in dairy, poultry and aquaculture.
As resistance spreads, standard drugs like ciprofloxacin fail for E. coli, so doctors turn to reserve carbapenems.
Now carbapenems are failing too: Klebsiella susceptibility to imipenem dropped from 58.5% to 35.6% by 2023.

history.text: India's worry about drug-resistant germs goes back more than a decade. In 2010 the government set up a National Task Force on AMR Containment. A national containment policy and the Jaipur Declaration followed. By 2012 Indian hospitals reported very high resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, the group that includes E. coli and Klebsiella. Many produced ESBLs, enzymes that break down common antibiotics. Resistance to carbapenems, a group of powerful reserve drugs, was rising. Authors called the subcontinent an epicentre of multidrug-resistant germs. In August 2012 Indian medical societies issued the Chennai Declaration. They asked for a national antibiotic policy. As first steps, they wanted strict control of over-the-counter sales and of hospital use. In 2013 India created Schedule H1 to restrict the sale of newer antibiotics. Studies later found weak enforcement, and buyers shifted to drugs outside the list. In April 2017 India adopted its National Action Plan on AMR. It used a One Health approach, treating human, animal and environmental use as one problem. In 2018 Kerala became the first state with its own plan, KARSAP, and its own surveillance network, KARS-NET. Yet ICMR's report, covered in September 2024, showed resistance kept rising from 2017 to 2023.

analogy.text: Think of weeding a garden with one spray. Most weeds die, but a few hardy ones survive and seed the next crop. Spray often, and soon the bed is mostly hardy weeds. Then you need a stronger spray.
analogy.breaks: Bacteria can also pass resistance genes directly to each other, so resistance can spread faster than seeding alone.

for_you.text: If you get typhoid, ciprofloxacin is unlikely to work. Over 95% of typhoid bacteria in ICMR data resisted its drug family. Take antibiotics only on a doctor's prescription, and don't push for them. Sale of newer antibiotics is restricted under Schedule H1, but enforcement is weak. In hospital, ask whether a culture test is planned.

misconception.myth: Antibiotic resistance means my body has become resistant to the drug.
misconception.fact: Bacteria become resistant, not people. Resistant germs can move between people, animals and the environment, which is why India's plan uses a One Health approach.

lesson.concept: How a susceptibility rate guides a doctor's antibiotic choice
lesson.big_idea: A susceptibility rate is the share of germ samples a drug still stops. Doctors often pick a drug before lab results arrive, so a lower rate means more first choices fail.

steps.title: A lab tests the germ
steps.text: A doctor sends a sample, like blood or urine, to a lab. The lab grows the bacteria and adds a drug. If growth stops, the germ is 'susceptible'. If it keeps growing, it is 'resistant'.

steps.title: Many tests become one percentage
steps.text: ICMR's surveillance network collects such results from hospitals across India. The share of samples a drug stops is its susceptibility rate. E. coli and Klebsiella were the bacteria most often found.

steps.title: Doctors often guess first
steps.text: Lab results take time, and a very sick patient cannot wait. So doctors start the drug most likely to work, based on known rates. A lower rate means more first guesses fail.

steps.title: Failure pushes to reserve drugs
steps.text: When the first drug fails, doctors switch to stronger reserve drugs called carbapenems, such as imipenem and meropenem. But these are falling too, so fewer backup options remain.

example.setup: Imagine a hospital where 100 patients have serious E. coli infections. Doctors start all of them on piperacillin-tazobactam before lab results arrive.

lines.label: 2017 first guess
lines.note: Using the 2017 rate, the drug worked for most.

lines.label: 2023 first guess
lines.note: Now fewer than half are helped.

lines.label: First drug fails
lines.note: Up from about 43 in 2017.

lines.label: Switch to imipenem
lines.note: Simplified; resistance often clusters in the same germs, so real odds may be worse.

lines.label: Still no working drug
lines.note: They need yet another option.

example.result: In this made-up hospital, first-drug failures rose from about 43 to 58 out of 100. Even after a reserve drug, about 22 patients still lack one that works.

apply.text: This is why ICMR's numbers matter. In 2023, piperacillin-tazobactam stopped only 42.4% of E. coli samples, so a first guess fails more often than it works. Klebsiella fared worse: imipenem stopped just 35.6%. For typhoid, over 95% resistance means ciprofloxacin is no longer a reliable first choice.

practice.q: Same hospital, but the 100 patients have Klebsiella in 2023. Piperacillin-tazobactam works for 26.5%, meropenem for 37.6%. How many lack a working drug after both?
practice.answer: First drug: 26.5% of 100 ≈ 27 helped, so 100 − 27 = 73 fail. Second drug: assume 37.6% of 73 ≈ 27 helped. 73 − 27 = 46 patients still lack a working drug, more than double the 22 in the E. coli example.

takeaways: A susceptibility rate is the share of germ samples a drug still stops; lower means more failed first guesses.
ICMR data shows common and reserve antibiotics stopping far fewer E. coli and Klebsiella infections than in 2017.
Watch ICMR's next annual report, and whether Schedule H1 and the national AMR plan are enforced.

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jisse yeh saare numbers samajh aate hain: susceptibility rate. Yeh germ samples ka woh hissa hai jise koi drug ab bhi rok paati hai. scenes.show: Susceptibility rate = share a drug stops
scenes.speak: अब वो एक idea जिससे ये सारे numbers समझ आते हैं: susceptibility rate। ये germ samples का वो हिस्सा है जिसे कोई drug अब भी रोक पाती है। Step one: lab patient के sample से bacteria उगाती है और drug डालती है। अगर growth रुक गई, तो germ susceptible है। अगर नहीं, तो resistant।

scenes.say: Step two: ICMR ka network kai hospitals ke results jod kar ek percentage banata hai. Step three: bahut beemar patients lab results ka intezaar nahi kar sakte, isliye doctors pehle ek likely drug shuru karte hain. Rate jitna kam, utne zyada first guesses fail. Step four: phir doctors carbapenems jaisi reserve drugs par switch karte hain.

scenes.speak: Step two: ICMR का network कई hospitals के results जोड़ कर एक percentage बनाता है। Step three: बहुत बीमार patients lab results का इंतज़ार नहीं कर सकते, इसलिए doctors पहले एक likely drug शुरू करते हैं। Rate जितना कम, उतने ज़्यादा first guesses fail। Step four: फिर doctors carbapenems जैसी reserve drugs पर switch करते हैं।

Sabko piperacillin-tazobactam di jaati hai. 2017 ke rate par, chhappan point aath percent, lagbhag 57 ko fayda hota hai. 2023 ke rate par, bayalis point chaar, lagbhag 42 ko. scenes.speak: चलिए एक example करते हैं। मान लीजिए एक hospital में 100 patients को serious E. coli infection है। सबको piperacillin-tazobactam दी जाती है। 2017 के rate पर, छप्पन point आठ percent, लगभग 57 को फ़ायदा होता है। 2023 के rate पर, बयालीस point चार, लगभग 42 को। तो 58 first guesses fail होते हैं, पहले लगभग 43 होते थे।

Matlab do koshishon ke baad bhi 22 patients ke paas koi kaam karne wali drug nahi. Asli haalat isse buri ho sakti hai, kyunki resistance aksar unhi germs mein ikattha hoti hai.

scenes.say: Ab khud try kijiye. Wahi hospital, lekin germ hai Klebsiella. Piperacillin-tazobactam chhabbis point paanch percent par kaam karti hai: lagbhag 27 ko fayda, 73 fail. Maan lijiye meropenem unmein se saintis point chhah percent par kaam karti hai: lagbhag 27 aur. Bache 46 jinke paas koi kaam karne wali drug nahi.

scenes.say: Aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? Agar aapko typhoid hota hai, toh ciprofloxacin ke kaam karne ke chances kam hain. Antibiotics sirf doctor ke prescription par lijiye, aur unke liye zor mat daaliye. Hospital mein poochiye ki kya culture test plan hai, taaki drug germ se match kare.

stories.headline: Bisleri water sample fails safety test; FSSAI approves prosecution
stories.question: Is bottled water safe after a Bisleri sample failed India's food safety test?
stories.dek: One Bisleri water sample failed two lab tests for chemicals that FSSAI classes as carcinogens. The levels and batch details were not published, so nobody outside the regulator can yet judge the risk to people who drank it.

so_far.text: Bisleri brought bottled water to India in 1965, though accounts differ on the details. Packaged water is regulated by FSSAI, India's national food regulator. Until October 2024, makers also needed certification from BIS, the national standards body. The government then dropped that requirement. In November 2024, FSSAI put packaged water in its high-risk food category, with yearly inspections and third-party audits. A new FSSAI testing scheme for packaged water took effect in January 2026.

what_happened.text: On 22 November 2026, Mint, the Times of India and the Indian Express reported that FSSAI had sanctioned prosecution of Bisleri International. A packaged water sample taken from the company's premises was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The first lab found bromate above the prescribed limit. Bisleri appealed, and a referral lab also declared the sample unsafe, citing PAHs. FSSAI also sanctioned prosecution of four other firms and suspended two firms' licences. No levels, batch number, city or sampling date were published. The Tribune reports that Bisleri was told to withdraw the batch; this is not yet confirmed.

steps.text: FSSAI sets a maximum limit for harmful substances in packaged water. A sample above a limit is declared unsafe.
The first lab found bromate above its prescribed limit, so the Bisleri sample failed.
Bisleri used its right to appeal, so a referral lab retested the sample. It also found it unsafe, citing PAHs.
With two labs finding it unsafe, and both chemicals classed as carcinogens, FSSAI sanctioned prosecution.
The case came after BIS certification stopped being mandatory in October 2024 and FSSAI made packaged water a high-risk food.

history.text:
Bottled water came to India in 1965 with Bisleri, a brand named after the Italian chemist Felice Bisleri. Sources differ on the exact details of that start. In 1969 Parle, led by Ramesh Chauhan, bought the brand. Chauhan later took over Parle Exports, which is now Bisleri International.

The industry grew large. India's bottled water market was worth about $3.79 billion in 2023, and the Trade Promotion Council of India projects about $8.9 billion by 2030. Yet about 80% of the industry is unorganised, meaning it sits outside large, formal companies.

For years, packaged water makers had to follow two sets of rules: FSSAI's food rules and the BIS standard, IS 14543. The industry asked for simpler norms. In October 2024 the government removed mandatory BIS certification. An FSSAI official called this a potential regulatory gap, because one layer of checking had gone.

FSSAI then tightened its own checks. On 29 November 2024 it placed packaged drinking and mineral water in its high-risk food category. That brought annual inspections and third-party audits. In December 2025 it issued a new testing scheme for packaged water, in force from January 2026.

This tighter system is the background to the November 2026 decision to prosecute Bisleri International.

lesson.concept: How a safety limit decides 'unsafe' water
lesson.big_idea: A regulator sets a maximum amount for each harmful substance. A sample above that limit is declared unsafe. How risky it actually is depends on how far over it is, and for how long people drink it.

steps.title: The regulator sets limits
steps.text: For packaged water, FSSAI has a prescribed limit for substances such as bromate. A limit is the most of a substance allowed in a litre. Limits are usually set below the level where harm is expected, to leave a safety margin.

steps.title: A lab compares sample to limit
steps.text: An official takes a sample, in this case from Bisleri's own premises. A lab measures each substance and compares it with the limit. Anything above the limit fails, even by a small amount.

steps.title: The company can appeal
steps.text: A failed result can be challenged. Bisleri used this right, so the sample went to a referral lab, a second lab that retests it. Here the referral lab also declared the sample unsafe, citing PAHs.

steps.title: Confirmed failure leads to action
steps.text: Once a sample is declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the regulator can act. FSSAI sanctioned prosecution, which means approval to take the company to court.

steps.title: Hazard is not risk
steps.text: A carcinogen is a substance that can cause cancer: that is its hazard. Risk depends on dose: how much, how often, and for how long. FSSAI published no levels, so the risk here cannot be judged.

example.setup: Imagine a water bottler's sample is tested for one chemical. Assume the limit is 10 units per litre, and the first lab measures 14 units.

lines.label: Compare to limit
lines.calc: 14 units vs assumed limit of 10 units
lines.note: 14 is higher than 10, so the sample fails.

lines.label: How far over
lines.note: The excess shows the size of the breach.

lines.label: As a percentage
lines.note: A percentage makes breaches easy to compare.

example.result: The rule is simple: over the limit means unsafe. But only the measured numbers tell you whether a sample was slightly over or far over, and so how worried drinkers should be.

apply.text: In the Bisleri case, the first lab found bromate above the limit. After the appeal, the referral lab also declared the sample unsafe, citing PAHs, and FSSAI sanctioned prosecution. But FSSAI published no measured levels. So we cannot do the 'how far over' step from our example, and the real risk to drinkers is still unknown.

practice.q: Keep the assumed limit of 10 units. Brand B's sample measures 10.5 units; brand C's measures 25 units. Which fail, and by how much?
practice.answer: Both fail, because both are above 10. Brand B: 10.5 − 10 = 0.5 units; 0.5 ÷ 10 = 5% over. Brand C: 25 − 10 = 15 units; 15 ÷ 10 = 150% over. Both get the same label, 'unsafe', but the gaps are very different.

scenes.speak: कौन क्या कह रहा है? FSSAI कहता है sample unsafe है, और दोनों chemicals carcinogen classed हैं। Reports आने तक Bisleri ने जवाब नहीं दिया था, लेकिन appeal की थी। 2024 में industry simple rules चाहती थी, और FSSAI के एक official ने potential regulatory gap की बात की थी।

scenes.say: Ek aam galti: yeh sochna ki carcinogen label ka matlab hai har ghoont se cancer hoga. Label batata hai ki substance kya kar sakta hai. Asli risk is par depend karta hai ki kitna maujood hai, aur kitne samay tak. FSSAI ne levels publish nahi kiye.
scenes.show: Carcinogen label is not a dose
scenes.speak: एक आम गलती: यह सोचना कि carcinogen label का मतलब है हर घूँट से cancer होगा। Label बताता है कि substance क्या कर सकता है। असली risk इस पर depend करता है कि कितना मौजूद है, और कितने समय तक। FSSAI ने levels publish नहीं किए।

scenes.say: Aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? Ab tak aap apni Bisleri bottle check nahi kar sakte: na batch, na city, na date publish hui, aur withdrawal bhi confirm nahi hai. Packaged water ki saal mein ek baar inspection hoti hai, lekin Karnataka survey ishara karta hai ki sealed bottle koi guarantee nahi hai.
scenes.show: You can't check your bottle yet
scenes.speak: आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? अब तक आप अपनी Bisleri bottle check नहीं कर सकते: न batch, न city, न date publish हुई, और withdrawal भी confirm नहीं है। Packaged water की साल में एक बार inspection होती है, लेकिन Karnataka survey इशारा करता है कि sealed bottle कोई guarantee नहीं है।

scenes.say: Ab lesson ko use karte hain. Bisleri ke case mein hum nahi nikaal sakte ki sample limit se kitna upar tha, kyunki koi level publish nahi hua. Isliye peene walon ke liye asli risk ab bhi pata nahi hai.
scenes.image: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
scenes.speak: अब lesson को use करते हैं। Bisleri के case में हम नहीं निकाल सकते कि sample limit से कितना ऊपर था, क्योंकि कोई level publish नहीं हुआ। इसलिए पीने वालों के लिए असली risk अब भी पता नहीं है।

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? Order par Bisleri ka response. Batch number, sampling ki jagah aur naape gaye levels. Prosecution ka court tak pahunchna, aur baaki 4 firms ke naam. Aur kya sach mein batch withdrawal ka order hua tha.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? Order पर Bisleri का response। Batch number, sampling की जगह और नापे गए levels। Prosecution का court तक पहुँचना, और बाकी 4 firms के नाम। और क्या सच में batch withdrawal का order हुआ था।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Ek: legal limit se upar matlab unsafe. Do: Bisleri ka sample do labs mein fail hua aur FSSAI ne prosecution sanction kiya, lekin na levels publish hue na batch. Teen: Bisleri ka response, batch details, levels aur court case par nazar rakhiye.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। एक: legal limit से ऊपर मतलब unsafe। दो: Bisleri का sample दो labs में fail हुआ और FSSAI ने prosecution sanction किया, लेकिन न levels publish हुए न batch। तीन: Bisleri का response, batch details, levels और court case पर नज़र रखिए।

quiz.q: No change in Anthropic's sales was reported between 19 and 20 November, yet its shares fell about 10.8%. What best explains this?
options: Investors cut the multiple they will pay for its sales
Its IPO price was changed from $83 to $86.72
It lost a tenth of its customers in one day
quiz.why: Market value is sales times a multiple. With sales unchanged, a lower price means investors are paying a smaller multiple.

quiz.q: The Fed's rate is about 4% and its officials projected 3.7% inflation for 2026. Using the lesson, why might that rate not cool prices much?
options: The real rate is near zero, so borrowing barely costs more than prices rise
Higher rates will push up the price of gold
President Trump asked for higher rates
quiz.why: 4% minus 3.7% leaves a real rate near zero. Saving barely pays and borrowing barely hurts, so spending slows little.
